correctness.rationale: A reciprocal-closed divisor subset in N=2^a p selects exactly one binary mask over the a+1 distinct pairs (2^i,2^(a−i)p). Their sum x+p rev_(a+1)(x)=2^(a+1)p makes p=x/(2^(a+1)−rev(x)), with positive denominator and p<2^(a+1). Thus all prime completions for 1≤a≤9 are covered by 2^(a+1)−1 exact masks. An independently written direct bit-reversal loop with deterministic primality tests reproduced P1={3}, P2={7}, P3=∅, P4={31}, P5={11}, P6={127}, P7=P8=∅, P9={23,179}. Masks 943 and 895 give p=23 and p=179, respectively, with exact reciprocal closure and sums 2N. No inference beyond a=9 is claimed.

value.rationale: The least exponent at which one dyadic support admits two different odd-prime completions is a natural parameter-family branching invariant. It separates the known one-pair p=179 mechanism from the genuinely two-omission-pair p=23 mechanism; requires exhaustive exclusion of all p for a≤8, not simply discovering either known integer. It is a complete exact finite classification of a mathematically motivated initial parameter regime.
